summary: Peter von Bohlen was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp, Georg Freytag, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1825.

Peter von Bradke worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dorpat under Leo Meyer, at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and at Leipzig, Jena, and Giessen. He served as extraordinary professor at the University of Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

Peter von Köppen was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (circa 1809–1814) and the University of Tübingen (circa 1819–1821), later holding a post at the Ministry of State Property (circa 1837–1860).

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Heinz Bechert. She held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), the Mainz Academy (around 2002), and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (around 2012).

Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the University of Munich, and the ICRH.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and served as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a historian and sinologist educated at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He taught history at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and Harvard University from 1978, where he directed the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies from 1980 to 1986.

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious studies who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. Attested in 2010, he served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at Leeds.

Philip B. Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology educated at Columbia University. He held positions at Columbia as Adjunct Associate Professor, East Asian Library Librarian, and Lecturer, and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer between 1990 and 1996. Around 2008, he became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.

Philip Deslippe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He has been a graduate student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2020–2026), where he also served as a teaching associate (attested 2020).

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Daiun Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and the Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (circa 1970–1985), became the John A. O'Brien Professor at Notre Dame in 1985, and served as American Philosophical Association President (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago. He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies from 2010 to 2018.

Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and Syracuse University, and taught at the Dominican University of California from circa 1980 to 2017.

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies figure who earned a BA from Reed College and studied under Richard Baker. He taught at Naropa University, served as resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, head monk at Dharma Sangha, and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center.

Philipp André Maas is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He has held positions at Bonn, the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Leipzig.

Philippe Stern was a French scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Musée Guimet (1927–1965), the Musée de la parole et du geste (circa 1928–1938), and taught at the École du Louvre (1929–1965).
